# AI Pricing Statistics 2026: Models, Price Points and Trends

Source: https://lowob.com/research/ai-pricing-statistics-2026/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-11-16 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Revenue

> Summary: A sourced reference of AI pricing statistics for 2026. Hybrid pricing reached 37% of software companies, consumption pricing 42% and outcome pricing 23% of AI vendors, and AI credits 29%. AI product margins averaged 45% in 2025. Every figure is dated and sourced, and most come from investor or vendor surveys, which we label.

In 2026, 37% of software companies used hybrid pricing (Growth Unhinged, May 2026), consumption pricing reached 42% of AI companies and outcome pricing 23% (ICONIQ, July 2026), and AI product gross margins averaged 45% in 2025. Buyers lean towards metering: 42.9% prefer consumption pricing for GenAI features. Most figures here are surveys run by investors, analysts or vendors.

*Figure: Where this piece sits: the commercial line, where the build starts.*

This page collects the numbers. The analysis of what to do with them is in **lowob**'s pricing hub, [Seats, usage or outcomes](https://lowob.com/research/seats-usage-or-outcomes/), and in the explainers on [AI gross margin](https://lowob.com/research/ai-gross-margin-explained/) and [AI credits](https://lowob.com/research/ai-credits-explained/). Vendor prices were checked on the vendors' own pages on 16 November 2026, in US dollars.

## What are the headline AI pricing statistics for 2026?

Hybrid pricing is now the most common single answer, consumption and outcome pricing are both growing among sellers, and AI margins sit well below SaaS.

| Statistic | Figure | Source | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Software companies using hybrid pricing | 37%, up from 25% a year earlier | Growth Unhinged survey, 230+ companies | May 2026 |
| AI companies using consumption-based pricing | 42%, up from 35% six months earlier | ICONIQ, about 300 executives | July 2026 |
| AI companies using outcome-based pricing | 23%, up from 18% six months earlier | ICONIQ | July 2026 |
| Software companies offering AI credits | 29% | Growth Unhinged | May 2026 |
| Buyers preferring consumption pricing for GenAI features | 42.9% | The Futurum Group, 830 IT decision makers | April 2026 |
| Average AI product gross margin | 45% in 2025 | ICONIQ | July 2026 |
| Median target AI gross margin | About 50% | Growth Unhinged | May 2026 |
| Software companies that changed pricing or packaging in the past year | Three in four | Growth Unhinged | May 2026 |

## What pricing models do AI companies use?

Most combine models. ICONIQ found AI companies blend an average of 1.7 pricing models, and Growth Unhinged found more companies letting customers choose.

| Statistic | Figure | Source | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Companies blending pricing models, average number | 1.7 | ICONIQ | July 2026 |
| Companies letting customers choose between pricing models | 29%, up from 21% | Growth Unhinged | May 2026 |
| Per-seat adoption among companies above $150m annual recurring revenue | 29% | Growth Unhinged | May 2026 |
| Flat-fee adoption among companies below $5m annual recurring revenue | 37% | Growth Unhinged | May 2026 |
| AI-native SaaS companies offering usage-based pricing | 83% | Maxio survey, cited by Deloitte | November 2025 |
| AI companies catalogued by a billing vendor using some form of hybrid | "The majority" of 50+ | Metronome | April 2026 |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## What pricing do AI buyers prefer?

Buyers want metering for AI and predictability for core software, and they are cooling on outcome pricing for AI.

| Statistic | Figure | Source | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prefer consumption pricing for GenAI features | 42.9%, up 5.3 points | The Futurum Group | April 2026 |
| Prefer outcome-based pricing for GenAI features | 26.8%, down from 30.9% | The Futurum Group | April 2026 |
| Prefer consumption pricing for core software | 30.1%, down 5.8 points | The Futurum Group | April 2026 |
| Prefer outcome-based pricing for core software | 21.7%, up from 18.4% | The Futurum Group | April 2026 |
| Prefer fixed-price or perpetual for core software | 22.5%, up from 18.7% | The Futurum Group | April 2026 |
| Sellers saying AI spend comes from customers' technology or software budgets | 70% | Growth Unhinged | May 2026 |

Futurum's analyst read the split as a case for hybrids: stable subscriptions for the core, metering for AI.

## How fast are AI model prices falling?

Fast for a fixed level of performance, while agents use more tokens per task. The [inference cost explainer](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-ai-inference-cost/) explains why bills can still rise.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Price of GPT-3.5-level performance per million tokens | $20 (November 2022) to $0.07 (October 2024), more than 280-fold | Stanford HAI, AI Index 2025 | April 2025 |
| Annual price decline for a fixed performance level | 9 to 900 times a year, by task | Epoch AI | March 2025 |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5, input and output per million tokens | $2 and $10 | Anthropic API pricing | 16 November 2026 |
| Claude Haiku 5.5, input and output per million tokens (prompts to 100,000 tokens) | $0.10 and $0.50 | Anthropic API pricing | 16 November 2026 |
| Anthropic Batch API discount | 50% on input and output | Anthropic API pricing | 16 November 2026 |
| Tokens used by agents, compared with chat | About 4 times; multi-agent systems about 15 times | Anthropic engineering | June 2025 |

A shift away from seats, slower than vendors hope, with a large share of agent projects at risk.

| Agentic AI projects cancelled | More than 40% by the end of 2027 | Gartner, reported by Reuters | June 2025 |
| Internal AI productivity spend as a share of revenue at AI companies | 11% in 2025; 16% projected 2026 | ICONIQ | July 2026 |

Often enough that any list price should carry a date. Unit definitions changed at two major support vendors within ten weeks in 2026.

| Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Fin for about $3.6 billion | 15 June 2026 | Salesforce press release | 15 June 2026 |
| Zendesk resolution tiers introduced | 18 May 2026 | Zendesk Help Center | Checked 16 November 2026 |

| Major pricing structure changes at Cursor | Four in under two years | Metronome | April 2026 |

## How reliable are these statistics?

Treat them as directional. Growth Unhinged's survey was supported by Metronome, a billing vendor, and is self-reported. ICONIQ and Bessemer are investors, and their 2026 and 2027 margins are projections. Futurum did not disclose fielding dates in its release. Gartner's figures are forecasts. Vendor prices are list prices and change often; negotiated prices are usually lower. Where sellers and buyers disagree, as on outcome pricing, both can be true: more vendors offer it while fewer buyers say they prefer it.

## lowob takeaways

- **Hybrid is the norm.** Most AI companies combine a fixed fee with usage, credits or outcomes.
- **Buyers want metering for AI.** Preference for outcome pricing on GenAI features is falling.
- **Margins sit below SaaS.** Investor data puts AI products at about 25% to 60%.
- **Date every price.** Units and list prices changed at several large vendors in 2026.

## Common questions

### What percentage of AI companies use usage-based pricing?

ICONIQ's July 2026 survey of about 300 AI executives found consumption-based pricing at 42%, up from 35% six months earlier. Deloitte cited a Maxio survey finding 83% of AI-native SaaS companies offer usage-based pricing. The figures measure different things: ICONIQ counts the model in use, Maxio whether it is offered at all.

### How many software companies use hybrid pricing in 2026?

Kyle Poyar's Growth Unhinged survey of more than 230 software companies, published in May 2026, found 37% use a hybrid pricing model, up from 25% a year earlier. ICONIQ separately found AI companies blend an average of 1.7 pricing models. The survey was supported by Metronome, a billing vendor, and is self-reported.

### What is the average gross margin for AI products?

ICONIQ's July 2026 State of AI report put the average AI product gross margin at 45% in 2025, projected to rise to 53% in 2026 and 59% in 2027. Bessemer's August 2025 report put its fastest-growing AI start-ups at about 25%. SaaS Capital says SaaS licence revenue usually earns 80% to 85%.

### Do buyers prefer outcome-based pricing for AI?

Fewer do than a year ago. The Futurum Group's survey of 830 IT decision makers, released in April 2026, found preference for outcome-based GenAI pricing fell from 30.9% to 26.8%, while preference for consumption pricing rose to 42.9%. Futurum linked the fall to uncertainty about how to define and measure AI outcomes.

### How much do AI assistants cost per user for business?

As checked on vendors' pages on 16 November 2026, Microsoft 365 Copilot Business lists at $21 per user per month on annual billing, ChatGPT Business and Claude Team standard seats at $20, and Google includes Gemini in Workspace Business Standard at $14. Premium seats at OpenAI and Anthropic cost $100 per seat per month on annual billing.
